description: The TEST validator quartet FUNCTION TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD (ISO 15.90) / TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD (15.91) / TEST-NUMVAL (15.93) / TEST-NUMVAL-C (15.94). LIVE (P11 Step 6): the date pair is an if/else-if verdict chain (year before month before day; codes 0/1/2[/3] confirmed by D.31.3.8/9); the NUMVAL pair is a THREE-leg verdict - 0 (r1a) / the 1-based first-error position (r1b, incl. the verbatim '0 1'->3 embedded-space sub-note and the arithmetic-mode digit caps: 31 native, 34 SDIDI) / LENGTH+1 (r1c: zero-length, all-spaces, incomplete like ' +.') - realized as position-reporting scanners beside the value parsers (the TestNumvalF discipline). TEST-NUMVAL-C rides the ONE BindNumvalCFamily bespoke bind (the 15.68.3-r3 currency injection + the r4f ANYCASE fold, shared with NUMVAL-C). COBOL-2002 introductions. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the 1985 intrinsic functions (Amendment 1, §1989:A.2.4 Table 1) run TAN, UPPER-CASE ('| TAN | N1 | N | Tangent of N1 |', '| UPPER-CASE | A1 or X1 | X | All letters in the argument are set to uppercase |') with no TEST- function; §2002:15.73 reads 'The TEST-DATE-YYYYMMDD function tests whether a date in standard date form (YYYYMMDD) is a valid date in the Gregorian calendar', §2002:15.74 'The TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD function tests whether a date in Julian date form (YYYYDDD) is a valid date in the Gregorian calendar', §2002:15.75 'The TEST-NUMVAL function verifies that the contents of argument-1 conform to the specification for argument-1 of the NUMVAL function' and §2002:15.76 the same of the NUMVAL-C function, and §2002:F.2 item 78 lists all four among 'Intrinsic functions. New intrinsic functions are'. §2014:15.83, §2014:15.84, §2014:15.86 and §2014:15.87 carry them, so 2014 = 2023; the 2023 text also dates the date pair itself (§2023:D.31.3.1: 'Two additional functions were added by ISO/IEC 1989:2002 as complements to these basic functions'). Below 2002 the D8 catalog window rejects by name+edition (COBOL1502).

    COMPUTE R2 = FUNCTION TEST-DAY-YYYYDDD(2024366)
